grants.program: Local Reporting Network (reporter-salary partnership for a yearlong investigation)
grants.amount: Reimburses reporter salary up to $80,000 for 2026 plus a benefits stipend; also funds some project expenses such as travel and public-records requests
grants.deadline: Winter 2026 cohort: rolling, letters of interest due Oct 15, 2026; Spring 2027 cohort: Jan 25, 2027 11:59 pm ET
grants.eligibility: Local and regional newsrooms may apply with a proposal; local/regional offices of national outlets are not eligible. NowKalamazoo is an independent local newsroom, so it meets the stated requirement.
beats: Surveillance, data centers and tech accountability
grants.why: The R&O series (6 stories in Sept 2026, charge records by race and residence) is exactly the data-driven yearlong accountability investigation this network funds; a follow-on project on policing/camera surveillance (Flock stories Feb and Aug 2026) is a second pitch. Page also says funding covers public-records request costs.
grants.fitReason: Funds a dedicated reporter on one investigation; direct match to a just-published, race-disparity data investigation.
grants.contactNote: ProPublica's page tells interested editors/reporters to email a program address, but the address is obfuscated in the fetched page; read it from the portal page directly.

grants.amount: RFA pays 50% of salary in year one (up to $27,500; $30,000 for very experienced journalists), 33% in year two, 20% in optional year three; host raises the rest. 80 new positions nationally per Sept 2026 trade coverage.
grants.deadline: Oct 19, 2026 (window opened Sept 14, 2026); winners announced Jan 19, 2027; corps member starts second Monday of July 2027
grants.eligibility: Any news organization, nonprofit or for-profit, committed to objective local journalism. Requirements: proposed beat fills an important need; publishing at least one year; high-quality editing; pays a living wage per the MIT calculator; agrees to fundraise its share. NowKalamazoo appears to meet publishing-time and nonprofit status; living-wage and editing standards must be confirmed by the newsroom.
beats: Northside News (historically Black neighborhood) and Eastside
Housing and homelessness (Uncovering the Housing Crisis, Housing Briefs)
grants.why: Policies & Power has 251 lifetime posts (15 in 2026) and housing coverage fell to 1 story in 2026 versus 20 Housing Briefs lifetime, a clear under-covered beat a corps member could own; R&O shows demand for a dedicated accountability reporter. Also pairs with WMU and Kalamazoo College student pipeline.
grants.fitReason: A funded full-time reporter on a defined beat; deadline is 19 days out.
grants.contactNote: Email is the only contact listed on RFA's Contact Us page; no named person published.

grants.amount: Not published on the guidelines page

notes: Post counts come from the WordPress REST API on 2026-09-30: 119 posts dated 2026-01-01 onward (X-WP-Total: 119, 2 pages). Category counts for 2026 were tallied from those 119 posts; lifetime counts are the site's category totals (Policies & Power 251, Northside News 32, Nonprofit Spotlight 42, Beyond Bullets 26, Housing Briefs 20, Election News 42, Election Briefs 28, Election Guides 10). Stories/COVID-19 categories are legacy archives and ignored.

Some beats the client named could not be measured as categories in 2026: the grocery price tracker returned no matching post titles through the API (likely a data page, not posts), and the public-meeting directory and GitHub repo are not WordPress posts. Counts for surveillance (4) and transparency (8) are title and category matches, not a dedicated category.

Not included as grants because they fail eligibility or have no open process as verified: Lenfest AI Collaborative and Fellowship (applications closed; program targets metro, local TV and statewide outlets, $5M OpenAI commitment announced Sept 2026); Knight Foundation (no always-open application, funding arises through relationships); MacArthur (Local News initiative, not a broad invitation to new applicants); American Journalism Project (no public application process found); Press Forward Northern Michigan (Grand Traverse region); Press Forward Colorado and California chapters (out of state); LION consulting for for-profit news businesses (NowKalamazoo is nonprofit).
Obfuscated addresses: ProPublica contact email, Joyce general inquiry email and FIJ email are obfuscated in the pages as fetched; no addresses were guessed.
Time-sensitive: NIHCM Oct 2, 2026; ProPublica LOI Oct 15, 2026; Report for America Oct 19, 2026; Gilmore Nov 2, 2026 (pre-contact needed 4 weeks ahead, so effectively tight); Joyce Dec 1, 2026.
unverified: Pulitzer Center: official program page returned 403; amount, deadline and contact email come from NewsFuel (newsfuel.org/opportunities/10) and search snippets. Search snippets also quoted a May 16, 2026 deadline, which conflicts with the 'rolling' listing.
Park Foundation deadlines (Jan 7, 2027 and prior quarterly dates) are from a secondary listing; the Park site did not show dates or amounts.
FIJ next deadline (Jan 29 or 30, 2027) is not yet published by FIJ. Indiegraf's list showed different 2026 dates (Sept 8/11) than FIJ's own page (Sept 14); FIJ's page was used.

Google News Initiative, INN and LION GNI programs: LION's Sustainability Audits and Funding (up to $20,000, LION member six months) and INN GNI pass-through grants appear in search results, but the only fetched LION page is from 2023 and no current 2026 or 2027 round was verified. NowKalamazoo received GNI money via Indiegraf.
Democracy Fund ($4 million multi-year grants to newsrooms centering people of color) and Press Forward local funders: no open application found.

Kellogg Foundation (Battle Creek, rolling LOI process), Mott Foundation (Flint), Michigan Humanities (Humanities and Bridging Michigan grants closed pending federal FY26 budget), Michigan Health Endowment Fund (health nonprofits, not journalism) and Michigan Arts and Culture Council: no journalism program or open call verified, so not scored.

Meta platform funds, Microsoft/OpenAI direct newsroom funds, National Press Foundation, Center for Cooperative Media (only collaboratives or travel grants of $500 to $1,000 found), Investigative Editors & Reporters (individual fellowships) and News Revenue Hub (services, not grants): no eligible open grant program for a local nonprofit newsroom found.
Report for America living-wage and editing standards: NowKalamazoo's compliance is not verifiable from public data.
KCF contact is 'Kari' with no surname or title beyond Community Impact Officer; Round 1 2027 dates not yet posted.
